name: Mpi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Sittichai. 1984. Phrases and clauses in the Mpi language at Ban Dong, Phrae Province (Mahidol thesis; named in Wikipedia further reading; not online)
earlier_scan.note: Mpi described as 6-tone Loloish (Wikipedia); stress statement not read; Sittichai 1984 thesis may cover it

sources.citation: Sittichai, Sah-Iam. 1984. Phrases and clauses in the Mpi language at Ban Dong, Phrae Province. MA thesis, Mahidol University (Institute of Language and Culture for Rural Development), 251 pp. scan.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1.6 'Transcriptions of the Mpi language' (thesis pp. 12-28 = PDF pp. 40-56) gives initials, vowels, six tones on monosyllables in isolation (after Harris in the 1976 dictionary), tone sandhi, final consonants and voice quality, enclitics and pronoun inflection; no mention of stress or accent. Secs. 3.1.5 and 6.7 'Prominence' (thesis pp. 82, 129-130) describe phrase-level emphasis by 'a high pitch or a loud voice on that element' or by particles, not word stress. The abstract explicitly defers phonology to further study.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Mpi language' (accessed 2026-09-17); Glottolog 5.3 languoid page mpii1239.
sources.note: Wikipedia repeats the SOWL tone/phonation table; nothing on stress. Glottolog lists Sittichai 1984 as the only descriptive reference; Grambank (JG) codes Mpi from Sittichai 1984 alone.

sources.citation: Ladefoged, Peter & Ian Maddieson. 1996. The Sounds of the World's Languages. Oxford: Blackwell, pp. 315-317 (Table 9.14, Mpi).
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Mpi cited for six tones each combinable with modal or stiff (laryngealized) voice on the syllable si (12 meanings).

sources.citation: UCLA Phonetics Lab Archive, Mpi (mpz): 1976 word-list recordings of Srinuan Duanghom by Peter Ladefoged (49 items). http://archive.phonetics.ucla.edu/Language/MPZ/
sources.note: Word list labelled only for tone and voice quality (6 tones x regular/tense voice); no stress information.
